existing_copy_for_context_only.medium: FBI documents summarized by TrumpFile place agents in Donald Trump’s office in early April 1981 to discuss Atlantic City casinos and organized crime. Trump said he would cooperate if he entered the casino business, and later suggested using undercover agents at a casino. The FBI drafted a proposal and scheduled another meeting.
existing_copy_for_context_only.long: FBI records summarized by TrumpFile describe an April 1981 meeting between Donald Trump, two agents, and informant Daniel Sullivan, a labor consultant to Trump who owned Atlantic City property Trump wanted for a casino. The discussion concerned casino licensing and organized crime; Trump said he was wary of criminal elements and of the background scrutiny required to obtain a license. He told agents Damon Taylor and Walt Stowe that he would cooperate if he moved ahead in Atlantic City. At a June meeting, Trump said he wanted to cooperate during construction and after opening and suggested filling the casino with undercover agents. Taylor then contacted FBI offices to prepare an undercover proposal, which records describe as nearly complete before agents scheduled a third meeting for October 1.
